components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 别: 制 is cutting to shape, then to make and to control.
月 (moon / flesh) — on the left, likely a squashed 舟 (boat) in 服, not a moon or body part. Dictionary story: a person 卩 putting on a coat 月.
卩 (kneeling person) — on the right, with 又 (hand). The old picture is a hand pressing someone down, 'submit'; clothes (衣服) and service (服务) came later.

example.hanzi: 警察穿着蓝色的制服。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá chuānzhe lánsè de zhìfú.
example.english: The police officer is wearing a blue uniform.
example.fact: 制服 covers two distinct senses under one written form — the noun "uniform" (school, police, military) and the verb "to subdue, bring under control" — with 制 contributing a sense of regulation and control to both: a regulated garment on one hand, and controlling a person on the other.

examples.hanzi: 学校要求学生每天穿制服。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào yāoqiú xuésheng měi tiān chuān zhìfú.
examples.english: The school requires students to wear uniforms every day.

examples.hanzi: 她穿着护士的制服，在医院里工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā chuān zhe hùshi de zhìfú, zài yīyuàn lǐ gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works in the hospital wearing a nurse's uniform.

components.note: 土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 块; 坏 first meant to collapse, as of a wall of earth.
不 (bù) is only a stand-in for the old sound part 褱 (huái); a loose clue for huài.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 撒谎是一件坏事。
example.pinyin: Sāhuǎng shì yí jiàn huàishì.
example.english: Lying is a bad thing to do.
example.fact: 坏事 pairs the everyday adjective 坏 ("bad, broken") with 事 ("matter, affair") to name a wrongdoing, mirroring its direct opposite 好事 ("a good deed") — both built from the same simple adjective-plus-"matter" pattern.

examples.hanzi: 他总是做好事，从不做坏事。
examples.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì zuò hǎoshì, cóng bú zuò huàishì.
examples.english: He always does good deeds and never bad ones.

examples.hanzi: 坏事传得比好事快。
examples.pinyin: Huàishì chuán de bǐ hǎoshì kuài.
examples.english: Bad news travels faster than good news.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 桌, 板: 查 first meant a raft of wood. 查 also gives 渣 zhā and 楂 zhā.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 警方终于查出了真相。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zhōngyú cháchū le zhēnxiàng.
example.english: The police finally found out the truth.
example.fact: 查 alone just means "to check, look into," but attaching the result-complement 出 ("out") turns it into "to check and succeed in finding out" — a common Chinese pattern where a bare verb needs a complement like 出/到/见 to confirm the action actually succeeded, not just that it was attempted.

examples.hanzi: 医生还没有查出他生病的原因。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng hái méiyǒu chá chū tā shēngbìng de yuányīn.
examples.english: The doctor hasn't yet found out the cause of his illness.

examples.hanzi: 电脑里的错误很快就被查出来了。
examples.pinyin: Diànnǎo lǐ de cuòwù hěn kuài jiù bèi chá chūlái le.
examples.english: The error in the computer was quickly found.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 这扇门是自动的。
example.pinyin: Zhè shàn mén shì zìdòng de.
example.english: This door is automatic.
example.fact: 自动 literally builds "self" (自) + "move" (动) — "moving by itself" — the same transparent "self-X" pattern recurs in common words like 自己 ("oneself") and 自然 ("nature," literally "self-so"), a productive prefix worth recognizing across many compounds.

examples.hanzi: 这台洗衣机可以自动关机。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái xǐyījī kěyǐ zìdòng guān jī.
examples.english: This washing machine can shut off automatically.

examples.hanzi: 没有人要求他，他是自动来帮忙的。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén yāoqiú tā, tā shì zìdòng lái bāngmáng de.
examples.english: Nobody asked him; he came to help voluntarily.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.hanzi: 她要去法院打官司。
example.pinyin: Tā yào qù fǎyuàn dǎ guānsi.
example.english: She's going to court to file a lawsuit.
example.fact: 院 in 法院 doesn't mean "hospital" — its core sense is simply "an enclosed institutional compound" (walled by 阝, the mound/enclosure radical), the same root shared by 医院 ("hospital") and 学院 ("college"), each just a different institution housed within walls.

examples.hanzi: 他们的案子下周在法院开庭。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen de ànzi xià zhōu zài fǎyuàn kāitíng.
examples.english: Their case will be heard in court next week.

examples.hanzi: 法院已经做出了判决。
examples.pinyin: Fǎyuàn yǐjīng zuò chū le pànjué.
examples.english: The court has already issued its ruling.

components.note: 二 (two) — the bottom bars. 丑 is an old calendar sign (the second branch) later borrowed for 'ugly'. Memory aid: a clown with two stripes, as in 小丑.
刀 (knife) — the dictionary lists a knife-like stroke group. The shape does not explain 'ugly'; Memory aid only.

example.hanzi: 这只小鸭子很丑。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo yāzi hěn chǒu.
example.english: This little duckling is very ugly.
example.fact: 丑 is the opposite of 美, and the simplified form also stands for the old character 醜. In Chinese opera 丑 is the clown role, and 丑 is the second of the twelve Earthly Branches, linked to the Ox. 丑闻 means scandal.

examples.hanzi: 这个玩具长得有点丑。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wánjù zhǎng de yǒudiǎn chǒu.
examples.english: This toy looks a bit ugly.

examples.hanzi: 他在大家面前出丑了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàjiā miànqián chūchǒu le.
examples.english: He embarrassed himself in front of everyone.

components.note: 西 (west) — traditionally a bird settling on its nest at sunset, hence west; 西 turns up in 要 and 栖.
王 (jade, 玉 with its dot dropped) — a blade 刂 cutting two jades apart: to divide into groups, hence class or shift.
牙 (tooth) — a picture of interlocking teeth; 牙 also sounds out 芽 yá and 讶 yà.

example.hanzi: 他明年要去西班牙旅游。
example.pinyin: Tā míngnián yào qù Xībānyá lǜyóu.
example.english: He's going to travel to Spain next year.
example.fact: 西班牙 is mostly a phonetic transliteration of "España" — 西 ("west") happens to also fit the country's location relative to China, but the "-班牙" syllables were chosen for their sound rather than their meaning, the same transliteration strategy behind country names like 意大利 (Italy) and 加拿大 (Canada).

examples.hanzi: 西班牙的海边很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Xībānyá de hǎibiān hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: The seaside in Spain is beautiful.

examples.hanzi: 我正在学西班牙语。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhèngzài xué Xībānyá yǔ.
examples.english: I am learning Spanish.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.
扌 (hand) — hand radical — 播 is scattering seed by hand, then broadcasting.
番 (fān) — near sound — 播 is bō; 番 also sounds out 翻 fān and 潘 pān.

example.hanzi: 这场比赛会在网上直播。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài huì zài wǎngshàng zhíbō.
example.english: This match will be livestreamed online.
example.fact: 直播 literally means "straight, direct" (直) + "broadcast" (播) — broadcasting with no delay or edit — and the word slid seamlessly from television and radio into today's internet livestreaming without needing a new coinage, since the old TV-era term already captured the same "unedited, real-time" idea.

examples.hanzi: 今晚的音乐会会在网上直播。
examples.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de yīnyuèhuì huì zài wǎng shang zhíbō.
examples.english: Tonight's concert will be broadcast live online.

examples.hanzi: 她每个周末都在平台上做直播。
examples.pinyin: Tā měi ge zhōumò dōu zài píngtái shang zuò zhíbō.
examples.english: She does a livestream on the platform every weekend.

meanings: (fig.) to have nothing further to do (with sb or sth)

components.note: 手 (hand) — two hands joined in respect: bowing and saluting; compare 扌 in 拿 and 打.
手 (hand) — two hands joined in respect: bowing and saluting; compare 扌 in 拿 and 打.

example.hanzi: 我先走了,拜拜!
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiān zǒu le, báibái!
example.english: I'm heading out now, bye-bye!
example.fact: 拜拜 is a phonetic loan from English "bye-bye" — dictionaries list its main pronunciation as báibái (tone 2), which breaks from 拜's ordinary reading bài (as in 拜访, "to pay a visit"). Some sources also record a bāibāi (tone 1) variant, reflecting the word's status as a fairly recent borrowing rather than native vocabulary.

examples.hanzi: 明天见，拜拜！
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān jiàn, báibái!
examples.english: See you tomorrow, bye!

examples.hanzi: 他向我挥挥手，说了声“拜拜”。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒ huī huī shǒu, shuō le shēng "báibái".
examples.english: He waved at me and said "bye-bye."

meanings: to shift to an earlier date
to do sth ahead of time

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.

example.hanzi: 我们提前到了机场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen tíqián dào le jīchǎng.
example.english: We arrived at the airport ahead of schedule.
example.fact: 提前 works as both a verb ("to move something earlier," 会议提前了, "the meeting got moved earlier") and an adverb ("in advance," 提前通知, "notify in advance") without changing form. 提 contributes "to raise, lift" and 前 contributes "before, ahead," as if lifting an event forward in time.

examples.hanzi: 会议提前到了上午九点。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì tíqián dào le shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn.
examples.english: The meeting was moved up to nine in the morning.

examples.hanzi: 如果你想去，请提前告诉我。
examples.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ xiǎng qù, qǐng tíqián gàosu wǒ.
examples.english: If you want to go, please tell me in advance.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sunlight falling on everything: universal, common. 普 also sounds out 谱 pǔ.

example.hanzi: 他会说普通话。
example.pinyin: Tā huì shuō pǔtōnghuà.
example.english: He can speak Mandarin.
example.fact: 普 means widespread: 普通话 (Mandarin, literally 'common speech'), 普通 (ordinary), 普遍 (universal), 普及 (to popularize). It is the 'general' in 普通 and rarely stands alone.

examples.hanzi: 这个手机很普通。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī hěn pǔtōng.
examples.english: This phone is very ordinary.

examples.hanzi: 手机已经很普及了。
examples.pinyin: Shǒujī yǐjīng hěn pǔjí le.
examples.english: Mobile phones are already widespread.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室, 安; 宗 is the ancestral hall.
示 (altar) — 示 is an altar to the ancestors — a house with an altar means clan and religion.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.

example.hanzi: 他对不同的宗教很感兴趣。
example.pinyin: Tā duì bùtóng de zōngjiào hěn gǎn xìngqù.
example.english: He's very interested in different religions.
example.fact: 宗 pictures a roof (宀) over an altar (示) — a household's ancestral shrine — while 教 relates to instruction and discipline. 宗教 literally combines "ancestral worship" with "teaching," reflecting how the modern word for "religion" grew out of older vocabulary for lineage ritual and moral instruction.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家有很多不同的宗教。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā yǒu hěn duō bù tóng de zōngjiào.
examples.english: This country has many different religions.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该尊重每个人的宗教信仰。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi zūnzhòng měi ge rén de zōngjiào xìnyǎng.
examples.english: We should respect everyone's religious beliefs.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — insects and small creatures: 蚊, 蛇, 蜜; 蠢 is wriggling insects, then stupid.
春 (chūn) is a near sound match for chǔn.
贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 财, 费; 货 is goods that are traded.
化 (huà) — near sound — 货 is huò; 化 also sounds out 花 huā.

example.hanzi: 别听他的,他就是个蠢货。
example.pinyin: Bié tīng tā de, tā jiùshì gè chǔnhuò.
example.english: Don't listen to him, he's just an idiot.
example.fact: 货 ("goods, merchandise") shows up as a mildly dehumanizing suffix in a small family of insults — 蠢货 ("idiot"), 傻货 ("fool"), 废货 ("useless piece of junk") — literally treating the person being insulted as a defective product, worth noting since 货 alone is a completely neutral word.

examples.hanzi: 你别骂人，骂人蠢货很没礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié mà rén, mà rén chǔnhuò hěn méi lǐmào.
examples.english: Don't swear; calling people idiots is very rude.

examples.hanzi: 他在电影里被人骂作蠢货，觉得很委屈。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànyǐng lǐ bèi rén mà zuò chǔnhuò, juéde hěn wěiqu.
examples.english: In the movie he was called an idiot and felt wronged.

components.note: 土 (earth) — two people 从 sitting on the ground 土: to sit. Also in 座 zuò seat.
宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室; 牢 is a pen with a roof for cattle 牛, then a prison.
牛 (ox) — 牛 is cattle — kept inside for safety, so firm.

example.hanzi: 小偷因为偷东西被警察抓去坐牢了。
example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu yīnwèi tōu dōngxi bèi jǐngchá zhuā qù zuòláo le.
example.english: The thief was caught by the police and sent to prison for stealing.
example.fact: 坐牢 is a separable verb-object compound at heart: a time duration can slide directly into the middle of it in speech — 坐三年牢, literally "sit three years prison," meaning "serve three years in prison" — a flexibility English's fused verb "to imprison" doesn't allow. The same separability shows up in 关门 (also in this batch): 关了两次门, "closed the door twice."

examples.hanzi: 他因为偷东西差点坐牢。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi tōu dōngxi chàdiǎn zuòláo.
examples.english: He nearly went to prison for stealing.

examples.hanzi: 那个人坐牢三年，刚被放出来。
examples.pinyin: Nàge rén zuòláo sān nián, gāng bèi fàng chūlái.
examples.english: That man was in prison for three years and has just been released.

meanings: to take care that one does not

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 招 is to beckon with the hand.
召 (zhào) — near sound — 招 is zhāo; 召 also sounds out 照 zhào and 超 chāo.
口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.

example.hanzi: 他看到我就跟我打招呼。
example.pinyin: Tā kàndào wǒ jiù gēn wǒ dǎ zhāohu.
example.english: As soon as he saw me, he said hello to me.
example.fact: 招呼 almost always appears inside the fixed collocation 打招呼 ("to greet," literally "to strike a greeting") rather than standing alone as a bare verb — one of a large family of set phrases built around the near-empty light verb 打, alongside 打电话 ("to make a phone call") and 打篮球 ("to play basketball").

examples.hanzi: 请你先招呼一下客人。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ xiān zhāohu yíxià kèrén.
examples.english: Please attend to the guests first.

examples.hanzi: 我去招呼服务员来点菜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù zhāohu fúwùyuán lái diǎn cài.
examples.english: I'll call the waiter over to order.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — 山 is a mountain, as in 岛, 岁; 崩 is a mountain collapsing.
朋 (péng) — near sound — 崩 is bēng; 朋 also sounds out 棚 péng and 绷 bēng.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; 溃 is a river bursting its banks, so to collapse.
贵 (guì) — near sound — 溃 is kuì; 贵 also sounds out 馈 kuì.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,她整个人都崩溃了。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā zhěnggè rén dōu bēngkuì le.
example.english: Hearing this news, she completely fell apart.
example.fact: While 崩溃 can describe a literal physical collapse — a mountain giving way, a bridge, an economy — it's just as often used for a mental or emotional breakdown (心理崩溃, "psychological collapse"), extending the old image of a mountain crumbling (崩, built on 山) or a riverbank bursting (溃, built on 氵) onto inner experience.

examples.hanzi: 工作压力太大，他快要崩溃了。
examples.pinyin: Gōngzuò yālì tài dà, tā kuài yào bēngkuì le.
examples.english: The work pressure was too great, and he was about to break down.

examples.hanzi: 这座老桥已经开始崩溃了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lǎo qiáo yǐjīng kāishǐ bēngkuì le.
examples.english: This old bridge has started to collapse.

components.note: 木 (tree) — three trees make a dense forest; 林 is two trees, 森 sēn adds more.

example.hanzi: 森林里很安静。
example.pinyin: Sēnlín lǐ hěn ānjìng.
example.english: It is very quiet in the forest.
example.fact: 木, 林 and 森 show one, two and three trees, a neat example of repeating a character to show 'more'. 森 appears in 森林 (forest) and 阴森 (eerie). It is also a surname and part of many given names.

examples.hanzi: 夜里的树林有点阴森。
examples.pinyin: Yèlǐ de shùlín yǒudiǎn yīnsēn.
examples.english: The woods feel a bit eerie at night.

examples.hanzi: 亚马孙是世界上最大的热带森林。
examples.pinyin: Yàmǎxùn shì shìjiè shang zuì dà de rèdài sēnlín.
examples.english: The Amazon is the world's largest tropical forest.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical — 依 is to lean on someone.
衣 (yī) — same sound — 依 is yī, like 衣.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.

example.hanzi: 多年过去了,他依然爱着她。
example.pinyin: Duō nián guò le, tā yīrán àizhe tā.
example.english: Many years have passed, and he still loves her.
example.fact: 依然 is a more literary, written-register synonym of the everyday 还是/仍然 ("still") — it turns up far more often in narration, formal writing, and lyrics than in casual conversation, where a native speaker chatting with friends would default to 还是 or plain 还 instead.

examples.hanzi: 虽然下雨了，他依然去跑步。
examples.pinyin: Suīrán xià yǔ le, tā yīrán qù pǎobù.
examples.english: Even though it was raining, he still went running.

examples.hanzi: 这家老店依然保持着原来的味道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā lǎo diàn yīrán bǎochí zhe yuánlái de wèidào.
examples.english: This old shop still keeps its original flavor.

components.note: 平 (píng, flat) also lends its sound to 评 píng, 苹 píng and 坪 píng.
青 (qīng) hints at the -ing rhyme; same part in 清 请 情 晴 精. The 争 (contend) half is not a reliable clue.

example.hanzi: 湖面非常平静,像一面镜子。
example.pinyin: Húmiàn fēicháng píngjìng, xiàng yí miàn jìngzi.
example.english: The lake's surface is very calm, like a mirror.
example.fact: 平静 describes an absence of disturbance — calm water, a calm mood, a calm situation — and is distinct from 安静 ("quiet," about the absence of noise specifically): a room can be 安静 without necessarily being 平静, and vice versa, a distinction English's single word "calm/quiet" often collapses.

examples.hanzi: 听了一会儿音乐，她的心情平静了下来。
examples.pinyin: Tīng le yíhuìr yīnyuè, tā de xīnqíng píngjìng le xiàlái.
examples.english: After listening to music for a while, she calmed down.

examples.hanzi: 这里的生活很平静。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shēnghuó hěn píngjìng.
examples.english: Life here is very peaceful.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 右 is a hand 又 plus 口 (mouth) — as a memory aid, the right hand brings food to the mouth; 右 also sounds out 佑 yòu.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: following the edge. The part 力 stands in for 臱 in the traditional 邊.

example.hanzi: 邮局就在银行的右边。
example.pinyin: Yóujú jiù zài yínháng de yòubian.
example.english: The post office is right on the right side of the bank.
example.fact: 右边 mirrors 左边 ("left side") as one of Mandarin's basic spatial pairs, both built the same way from a direction word plus 边 ("side, edge") — 边 itself is a highly productive suffix that turns almost any location word into "the X side" (里边 "inside," 外边 "outside," 前边 "the front side").

examples.hanzi: 请从右边上车。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng cóng yòubian shàng chē.
examples.english: Please board from the right side.

examples.hanzi: 在中国，开车要靠右边走。
examples.pinyin: Zài Zhōngguó, kāi chē yào kào yòubian zǒu.
examples.english: In China, you drive on the right.

components.note: 乘 (chéng) — to ride; as a part it sounds out 剩 shèng.

example.hanzi: 我们乘飞机去上海。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chéng fēijī qù Shànghǎi.
example.english: We're taking a plane to Shanghai.
example.fact: 乘 is a formal 'ride', as in 乘车 (ride a vehicle), 乘客 (passenger) and 乘坐. It is also 'multiply': 三乘四等于十二, and 乘法 is multiplication.

examples.hanzi: 请乘客排队上车。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng chéngkè páiduì shàng chē.
examples.english: Passengers, please line up to board.

examples.hanzi: 你可以乘电梯到五楼。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ chéng diàntī dào wǔ lóu.
examples.english: You can take the elevator to the fifth floor.

components.note: 内 (inside) — a person or something entering 入 inside an enclosure 冂: inside, as in 内容.
衤 (clothing, 衣字旁) — clothes: 衬 shirt, 衫, 裙 skirt, 被 quilt; 裤 is trousers.
库 (kù) sounds exactly like 裤.

example.hanzi: 他把内裤和衣服分开洗。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ nèikù hé yīfu fēnkāi xǐ.
example.english: He washes his underwear separately from his clothes.
example.fact: 内裤 builds transparently from 内 ("inner, inside") plus 裤 ("trousers, pants") — literally "inner pants" — the same "inner-" prefix pattern behind 内衣 ("underwear" in general, literally "inner clothes") and 内心 ("one's inner heart/feelings").

examples.hanzi: 这条内裤是纯棉的，穿着很舒服。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo nèikù shì chúnmián de, chuān zhe hěn shūfu.
examples.english: These underpants are pure cotton and comfortable to wear.

examples.hanzi: 我给孩子买了几条新内裤。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi háizi mǎi le jǐ tiáo xīn nèikù.
examples.english: I bought a few new pairs of underpants for my child.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
勹 (wrap) — the visible part, a bent shape. Memory aid: a stooped figure under weight, wearing down over time — a long time, as in 好久.
灸 (jiǔ, moxibustion) — 久 is its sound part, same sound jiǔ. Another is 玖 jiǔ. The old picture of 久 is disputed.

example.hanzi: 他们结婚不久就有了孩子。
example.pinyin: Tāmen jiéhūn bùjiǔ jiù yǒu le háizi.
example.english: They had a child not long after they got married.
example.fact: 不久 almost always anchors to a reference point rather than floating freely the way 快 ("soon") can — 结婚不久 ("not long after marrying"), 不久以前 ("not long ago"), 不久以后 ("before long") — with the anchor coming either just before the phrase or built directly into it.

examples.hanzi: 不久以后，天就黑了。
examples.pinyin: Bùjiǔ yǐhòu, tiān jiù hēi le.
examples.english: Before long, it was dark.

examples.hanzi: 我来这里不久，还不太熟悉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ lái zhèlǐ bùjiǔ, hái bú tài shúxī.
examples.english: I haven't been here long and am not very familiar yet.

components.note: 冫 (water, ice) — 冲 is the simplified 沖: a water element (冫) beside 中, so water rushing; this form is a water cousin of 冰 and 冷.
中 (zhōng) — near sound — 冲 is chōng; 中 also sounds out 钟 zhōng.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and waves: 河, 海, 汤; 浪 is a wave.
良 (liáng) is a loose clue; also in 狼 láng, 朗 lǎng and 娘 niáng.

example.hanzi: 夏天他喜欢去海边冲浪。
example.pinyin: Xiàtiān tā xǐhuan qù hǎibiān chōnglàng.
example.english: In summer he likes to go surfing at the beach.
example.fact: 冲浪 literally means "to charge, rush at (冲) a wave (浪)" — a fairly recent coinage for the imported sport — and the same 冲 root now also covers "to rush online" in the internet-era slang 网上冲浪 ("to surf the web"), an extension that echoes English's own reuse of "surf" for browsing.

examples.hanzi: 海浪很大，很适合冲浪。
examples.pinyin: Hǎilàng hěn dà, hěn shìhé chōnglàng.
examples.english: The waves are big and perfect for surfing.

examples.hanzi: 他第一次冲浪就站起来了。
examples.pinyin: Tā dì-yī cì chōnglàng jiù zhàn qǐlái le.
examples.english: He stood up on his very first time surfing.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室; 牢 is a pen with a roof for cattle 牛, then a prison.
牛 (ox) — 牛 is cattle — kept inside for safety, so firm.

example.hanzi: 他在牢里待了三年。
example.pinyin: Tā zài láo lǐ dāi le sān nián.
example.english: He spent three years in prison.
example.fact: 牢 began as a pen for livestock, as the idiom 亡羊补牢 ('mend the pen after the sheep are lost') shows. It became 'prison' (坐牢) and 'firm' (牢固, 牢记 'remember firmly'). 牢骚 means grumbling.

examples.hanzi: 这把锁很牢固。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǎ suǒ hěn láogù.
examples.english: This lock is very sturdy.

examples.hanzi: 请把这句话牢牢记住。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè jù huà láolao jìzhù.
examples.english: Please remember this sentence firmly.

components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
大 (big/man) — the top part, as in 夫. Dictionary story: a big man wrapped in a long cloth, hence 'cover, set'; used in 外套 coat and 手套 glove.
镸 (long) — the bottom part, a long-hair variant of 長. Memory aid: a long cloth over a big person is a coat or cover.

example.hanzi: 外面很冷,记得穿外套。
example.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, jìde chuān wàitào.
example.english: It's cold outside, remember to wear a coat.
example.fact: 外套 literally means "outer (外) covering (套)" — 套 alone names any covering that slips over something else (手套, "gloves," literally "hand cover"; 枕套, "pillowcase") — so 外套 simply pictures a coat as the covering worn on the outside, over everything else.

examples.hanzi: 这件外套是新买的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn wàitào shì xīn mǎi de.
examples.english: This jacket is newly bought.

examples.hanzi: 天冷了，把外套穿上吧。
examples.pinyin: Tiān lěng le, bǎ wàitào chuān shàng ba.
examples.english: It's cold; put your coat on.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.

example.hanzi: 结婚是人生中的一件大事。
example.pinyin: Jiéhūn shì rénshēng zhōng de yí jiàn dàshì.
example.english: Getting married is a major event in life.
example.fact: 大事 sits opposite 小事 ("a trivial matter") on Mandarin's basic big/small scale for how much something matters — the two even combine into the paired saying 大事化小,小事化了 ("turn big problems into small ones, and small ones into nothing"), commonly offered as advice not to escalate a conflict.

examples.hanzi: 今天是个大事，我们要认真准备。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì ge dàshì, wǒmen yào rènzhēn zhǔnbèi.
examples.english: Today is a big deal, so we need to prepare carefully.

examples.hanzi: 别担心，没什么大事，只是小问题。
examples.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, méi shénme dàshì, zhǐshì xiǎo wèntí.
examples.english: Don't worry, it's nothing serious, just a small problem.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 口 is a mouth, as in 叫, 吗; 吓 is a shout that frightens.
下 (xià) — same sound — 吓 is xià, like 下.
土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 块; 坏 first meant to collapse, as of a wall of earth.
不 (bù) is only a stand-in for the old sound part 褱 (huái); a loose clue for huài.

example.hanzi: 那个声音把孩子吓坏了。
example.pinyin: Nàge shēngyīn bǎ háizi xiàhuài le.
example.english: That sound terrified the child.
example.fact: 坏 as a verb complement after 吓 doesn't mean "broken" here but marks an emotional or physical state pushed to an extreme — the same intensifying use of 坏 shows up in 累坏 ("exhausted, worn out") and 气坏 ("furious to the point of breaking"), a small family of "verb + 坏" compounds for a reaction pushed past its limit.

examples.hanzi: 突然的雷声把小狗吓坏了。
examples.pinyin: Tūrán de léishēng bǎ xiǎo gǒu xiàhuài le.
examples.english: The sudden thunder terrified the puppy.

examples.hanzi: 别吓坏孩子，他还小。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiàhuài háizi, tā hái xiǎo.
examples.english: Don't scare the child; he is still little.

components.note: 阝 (mound, hill) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound), as in 阳, 院; 陷 is falling into a pit.
臽 (xiàn) — same sound — 陷 is xiàn; 臽 also sounds out 馅 xiàn.
入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.

example.hanzi: 公司陷入了严重的财务危机。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī xiànrù le yánzhòng de cáiwù wēijī.
example.english: The company sank into a serious financial crisis.
example.fact: 陷入 is almost always followed directly by an undesirable abstract state — 陷入危机 ("sink into crisis"), 陷入困境 ("land in a predicament"), 陷入沉思 ("sink into deep thought") — rarely a literal hole, even though 陷 itself pictures exactly that: a pit (臽) dug into raised terrain (阝).

examples.hanzi: 他陷入了沉思。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiànrù le chénsī.
examples.english: He fell into deep thought.

examples.hanzi: 汽车陷入了泥里，开不出来。
examples.pinyin: Qìchē xiànrù le ní lǐ, kāi bù chūlái.
examples.english: The car sank into the mud and couldn't get out.

components.note: 手 (hand) — 手 as in 拿, 打, 拳; 掌 is the palm of the hand, then to control.
尚 (shàng) — near sound — 掌 is zhǎng; 尚 also sounds out 常 cháng, 堂 táng and 赏 shǎng.

example.hanzi: 他的手掌很大。
example.pinyin: Tā de shǒuzhǎng hěn dà.
example.english: His palm is very big.
example.fact: 掌 builds 手掌 (palm), 鼓掌 (to applaud), 掌声 (applause) and 掌握 (to master, grasp). It also means to hold power: 掌权.

examples.hanzi: 大家一起鼓掌。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ gǔzhǎng.
examples.english: Everyone applauds together.

examples.hanzi: 她把小鸟放在手掌上。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ xiǎo niǎo fàng zài shǒuzhǎng shang.
examples.english: She put the little bird on her palm.

components.note: 足 (foot) — marks feet and walking, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump, 路 road; 蹲 is squatting down on the feet.
尊 (zūn) — close sound: 蹲 dūn. 尊 also sounds out 遵 zūn and 樽 zūn.

example.hanzi: 他蹲在地上看蚂蚁。
example.pinyin: Tā dūn zài dì shàng kàn mǎyǐ.
example.english: He is squatting on the ground watching ants.
example.fact: 蹲 is to squat: 蹲下 (squat down), 蹲厕 (squat toilet). It extends to staying in one place for a long time, as in 蹲点 (to be stationed at a spot) and 蹲守 (to stake out).

examples.hanzi: 孩子蹲下来系鞋带。
examples.pinyin: Háizi dūn xiàlai jì xiédài.
examples.english: The child squatted down to tie his shoelaces.

examples.hanzi: 别蹲在路中间。
examples.pinyin: Bié dūn zài lù zhōngjiān.
examples.english: Don't squat in the middle of the road.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
衣 (clothes; 衤 on the left) — the outer garment.
毛 (fur) — a fur coat worn outside: the outside, the surface, then to show.

example.hanzi: 她刚发表了一篇新的论文。
example.pinyin: Tā gāng fābiǎo le yì piān xīn de lùnwén.
example.english: She just published a new academic paper.
example.fact: 发表 covers publishing writing (论文, "papers"; 文章, "articles") and also publicly voicing an opinion (发表意见, "to voice an opinion"). 发 contributes "to release, send out" and 表 contributes "to show, express" — together the word means "to release into view," equally at home with a printed paper or a spoken opinion.

examples.hanzi: 他在网上发表了自己的看法。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài wǎng shang fābiǎo le zìjǐ de kànfǎ.
examples.english: He published his opinion online.

examples.hanzi: 总统明天将发表重要讲话。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngtǒng míngtiān jiāng fābiǎo zhòngyào jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The president will deliver an important speech tomorrow.

components.note: 回 (return) — a swirl or whirlpool drawn as nested squares: it turns around and comes back.
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; here a hand seizing someone to pass judgment.
卩 (kneeling person) — with 又 hand: sentencing a kneeling prisoner, then answering back: repay, report.

example.hanzi: 父母对孩子的爱不求回报。
example.pinyin: Fùmǔ duì háizi de ài bù qiú huíbào.
example.english: Parents' love for their children doesn't seek anything in return.
example.fact: 回报 carries both a warmly reciprocal sense ("to repay a kindness," 回报社会, "to give back to society") and a sharper sense of retaliation or payback for wrongs, depending entirely on context — the same neutral "return" core (回, "to go back") stretched to cover both gratitude and revenge, where English usually needs different words for the two.

examples.hanzi: 努力学习一定会有回报的。
examples.pinyin: Nǔlì xuéxí yídìng huì yǒu huíbào de.
examples.english: Studying hard will surely pay off.

examples.hanzi: 他帮了我很多，我想找机会回报他。
examples.pinyin: Tā bāng le wǒ hěn duō, wǒ xiǎng zhǎo jīhuì huíbào tā.
examples.english: He helped me a lot, and I want to find a chance to repay him.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — marks cloth and garments, as in 衬, 衫, 补; 初 pairs it with 刀 knife: cutting cloth was the first step in making clothes, hence 'beginning'.
刀 (knife) — the cutting tool, as in 分 divide, 切 cut.

example.hanzi: 我们初次见面。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen chūcì jiànmiàn.
example.english: We are meeting for the first time.
example.fact: 初 means the start of something: 初次 (first time), 初中 (junior high), 月初 (beginning of the month), 初恋 (first love). 初一 is the first day of a lunar month; 大年初一 is Chinese New Year's Day.

examples.hanzi: 初中的时候我学了英语。
examples.pinyin: Chūzhōng de shíhou wǒ xué le Yīngyǔ.
examples.english: I learned English in junior high.

examples.hanzi: 我们月初开会。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yuèchū kāihuì.
examples.english: We have a meeting at the beginning of the month.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讲 is to talk and explain.
井 (jǐng) — near sound — 讲 is jiǎng; the old form had a different right side, so this is only a loose hint.

example.hanzi: 他明天要在大会上演讲。
example.pinyin: Tā míngtiān yào zài dàhuì shàng yǎnjiǎng.
example.english: He is going to give a speech at the conference tomorrow.
example.fact: 演讲 is reserved for a formal, prepared public speech — a lecture, a conference talk, a commencement address — while everyday chatting uses 讲话 or plain 说话 instead; reaching for 演讲 to describe a casual conversation would sound comically over-formal.

examples.hanzi: 他在毕业典礼上发表了演讲。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bìyè diǎnlǐ shang fābiǎo le yǎnjiǎng.
examples.english: He gave a speech at the graduation ceremony.

examples.hanzi: 这位教授经常去各地演讲。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi jiàoshòu jīngcháng qù gèdì yǎnjiǎng.
examples.english: This professor often travels to give lectures.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical; 俄 first meant sudden, and is now mostly 俄国 Russia.
我 (wǒ) — near sound — 俄 is é; 我 also sounds out 鹅 é and 饿 è.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 十九世纪的俄国出现了很多伟大的作家。
example.pinyin: Shíjiǔ shìjì de Éguó chūxiàn le hěn duō wěidà de zuòjiā.
example.english: Many great writers emerged from 19th-century Russia.
example.fact: 俄国 is the older, historically-flavored name for Russia, most natural in a historical or literary context like this one; present-day news and official contexts more often use the fuller transliteration 俄罗斯 — both trace their opening syllable to the same sound-match for "Ros-/Rus-."

examples.hanzi: 俄国的冬天又长又冷。
examples.pinyin: Éguó de dōngtiān yòu cháng yòu lěng.
examples.english: Winters in Russia are long and cold.

examples.hanzi: 他读了很多俄国文学作品。
examples.pinyin: Tā dú le hěn duō Éguó wénxué zuòpǐn.
examples.english: He has read many works of Russian literature.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 滴 is a drop of liquid, or to drip.
啇 (dí) — close sound: 滴 dī. 啇 also sounds out 敌 dí and 嫡 dí.

example.hanzi: 水龙头在滴水。
example.pinyin: Shuǐlóngtóu zài dī shuǐ.
example.english: The faucet is dripping.
example.fact: 滴 is both a verb (to drip) and a measure word for drops: 一滴水 (a drop of water). 点滴 means 'bit by bit', and in China 打点滴 is the common way to say getting an IV drip.

examples.hanzi: 窗外的雨一滴一滴地落下来。
examples.pinyin: Chuāng wài de yǔ yì dī yì dī de luò xiàlai.
examples.english: Outside the window the rain falls drop by drop.

examples.hanzi: 请给我滴两滴眼药水。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ dī liǎng dī yǎnyàoshuǐ.
examples.english: Please put two drops of eye drops in for me.

components.note: 广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 度 degree; 底 is the base of a house.
氐 (dī) is a close sound clue for dǐ; also in 低 dī and 抵 dǐ.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 钥匙就在椅子底下。
example.pinyin: Yàoshi jiù zài yǐzi dǐxia.
example.english: The key is right underneath the chair.
example.fact: 底下 names the physical space directly beneath something (椅子底下, "under the chair"), much like its close synonym 下面 — but 底 itself, built from 广 ("a structure") over the phonetic 氐, contributes a sense of "the very bottom or base," giving 底下 a slightly more literal "at the base of" flavor.

examples.hanzi: 猫躲在桌子底下。
examples.pinyin: Māo duǒ zài zhuōzi dǐxia.
examples.english: The cat is hiding under the table.

examples.hanzi: 他在树底下乘凉。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shù dǐxia chéngliáng.
examples.english: He is cooling off under the tree.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).
宀 (roof) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家, 室; 宜 is something fitting in a home.
且 (offering) — 且 is a stand for offerings (as in 祖), so 宜 is a proper offering in the house — suitable.

example.hanzi: 这条裙子很便宜,才五十块。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi hěn piányi, cái wǔshí kuài.
example.english: This skirt is really cheap, only fifty yuan.
example.fact: 便宜 hides two unrelated readings behind the same two characters: the common, everyday piányi ("cheap, inexpensive") and the rarer, more literary biànyí ("convenient, fitting"). This card corrects an earlier draft that surfaced the rare biànyí reading for this everyday word — the same dictionary-ordering trap that hit 告诉 and 东西 elsewhere in this deck.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的水果很便宜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de shuǐguǒ hěn piányi.
examples.english: The fruit in this shop is very cheap.

examples.hanzi: 别想占别人的便宜。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiǎng zhàn biéren de piányi.
examples.english: Don't try to take advantage of other people.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.

example.hanzi: 我们何时才能再见?
example.pinyin: Wǒmen héshí cái néng zàijiàn?
example.english: When will we be able to meet again?
example.fact: 何时 is the literary, written-register counterpart to everyday 什么时候 ("when"). 何 is a classical Chinese question word ("what, which") that survives today mostly in fixed formal or poetic expressions (何时, 为何 "why", 如何 "how"), rarely used alone in casual spoken Mandarin.

examples.hanzi: 你何时回来？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ héshí huílái?
examples.english: When will you come back?

examples.hanzi: 不知他何时才能完成这项工作。
examples.pinyin: Bù zhī tā héshí cái néng wánchéng zhè xiàng gōngzuò.
examples.english: I don't know when he will finish this work.

components.note: 戈 (spear) — two hands (廾) holding a spear: guarding against danger — hence warn, abstain, and 戒指 ring, from the old sense of guarding.

example.hanzi: 他决定戒烟了。
example.pinyin: Tā juédìng jièyān le.
example.english: He decided to quit smoking.
example.fact: 戒 means to give up a habit: 戒烟 (quit smoking), 戒酒 (stop drinking). It also appears in 戒指 (a finger ring), 警戒 (to be on alert) and 戒备 (to guard against).

examples.hanzi: 他在戒酒。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jièjiǔ.
examples.english: He is giving up drinking.

examples.hanzi: 孩子要戒掉玩手机的习惯。
examples.pinyin: Háizi yào jiè diào wán shǒujī de xíguàn.
examples.english: The child needs to quit the habit of playing on the phone.

meanings: (of a shop etc) to close (for the night or permanently)

components.note: 关 (close) — simplified from 關, a gate 门 with a bolt across it; 关 also means "concern", as in 关系.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 这家店晚上十点关门。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn wǎnshang shí diǎn guānmén.
example.english: This shop closes at ten at night.
example.fact: 关门 is a separable verb-object compound, like many two-character "verb + object" words in Chinese — a duration or aspect marker can slide between the two halves (关了门, "closed the door [already]"; 关过门, "has closed the door before"), a flexibility that a fused English verb like "to close" doesn't allow.

examples.hanzi: 商店九点就要关门了，我们快点去吧。
examples.pinyin: Shāngdiàn jiǔ diǎn jiù yào guānmén le, wǒmen kuài diǎn qù ba.
examples.english: The shop closes at nine, so let's hurry.

examples.hanzi: 睡觉前，别忘了关门。
examples.pinyin: Shuìjiào qián, bié wàng le guānmén.
examples.english: Don't forget to close the door before going to bed.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
纟 (silk, thread) — 纟 is the simplified 糸 (thread), as in 红, 给; 纪 first meant the thread end, then keeping record, as in 世纪.
己 (jǐ) — same sound, different tone — 纪 is jì; 己 also sounds out 记 jì.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这位演员的经纪人正在和电影公司谈判。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi yǎnyuán de jīngjìrén zhèngzài hé diànyǐng gōngsī tánpàn.
example.english: This actor's agent is negotiating with the film company.
example.fact: 经纪人 stacks three characters that each independently live in the "managing affairs" space — 经 ("to manage, to pass through"), 纪 ("to record, put in order"), and 人 ("person") — literally "a person who manages and organizes [transactions]," today covering everything from a sports agent to a real-estate broker.

examples.hanzi: 这位明星的经纪人很有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi míngxīng de jīngjìrén hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: This star's agent is very well known.

examples.hanzi: 我请了一个经纪人帮我卖房子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ qǐng le yí ge jīngjìrén bāng wǒ mài fángzi.
examples.english: I hired an agent to help me sell my house.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.
车 (cart) — simplified from 車, a wheeled cart seen from above. As a radical it marks vehicles: 转 turn, 轮 wheel, 较.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 商场旁边有一个很大的停车场。
example.pinyin: Shāngchǎng pángbiān yǒu yí gè hěn dà de tíngchēchǎng.
example.english: There's a very big parking lot next to the mall.
example.fact: 停车场 is built with total transparency from "to stop" (停) + "vehicle" (车) + "an open plot of ground" (场, the same 场 found in 广场, "public square," and 农场, "farm") — a "vehicle-stopping ground," one of the easiest three-character compounds to decode on sight.

examples.hanzi: 这个停车场晚上也开放。
examples.pinyin: Zhège tíngchēchǎng wǎnshang yě kāifàng.
examples.english: This parking lot is also open at night.

examples.hanzi: 停车场里已经没有空位了。
examples.pinyin: Tíngchēchǎng lǐ yǐjīng méiyǒu kòngwèi le.
examples.english: There are no free spaces left in the parking lot.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; 判 is to cut in half, so to separate and decide.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 判 is pàn; 半 means half.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 新, 析; 断 is to cut through, shown by the axe and threads cut.

example.hanzi: 很难判断他说的是不是真的。
example.pinyin: Hěn nán pànduàn tā shuō de shì bu shì zhēn de.
example.english: It's hard to judge whether what he says is true.
example.fact: 判 and 断 are already near-synonyms on their own — 判 ("to judge, to sentence") and 断 ("to decide, to cut off") — and 判断 doubles them into a single verb for weighing evidence and reaching a conclusion, the same synonym-doubling strategy behind compounds like 喜欢 and 应该.

examples.hanzi: 你要自己判断，不要轻易相信别人。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào zìjǐ pànduàn, bú yào qīngyì xiāngxìn biéren.
examples.english: You have to judge for yourself and not easily believe others.

examples.hanzi: 从他的表情可以判断他很生气。
examples.pinyin: Cóng tā de biǎoqíng kěyǐ pànduàn tā hěn shēngqì.
examples.english: From his expression you can tell he is very angry.

components.note: 成 (chéng) is a sound clue for 城 chéng, 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng: the same sound.
长 (long, grow) — simplified from 長, an old person with long hair. Read cháng "long" or zhǎng "to grow, elder".

example.hanzi: 孩子的成长需要父母的陪伴。
example.pinyin: Háizi de chéngzhǎng xūyào fùmǔ de péibàn.
example.english: A child's growth requires the companionship of their parents.
example.fact: 成长 differs from the more physical 长大 ("to grow up, get bigger") by leaning toward development and maturation as a process — often used for a person's character, a company's business, or a country's economy "growing," while 长大 stays anchored to literal physical growth, mostly of children.

examples.hanzi: 孩子在爱中慢慢成长。
examples.pinyin: Háizi zài ài zhōng mànmàn chéngzhǎng.
examples.english: Children grow up gradually in love.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司成长得很快。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī chéngzhǎng de hěn kuài.
examples.english: This company is growing very fast.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 科学家们正在做一项新的试验。
example.pinyin: Kēxuéjiāmen zhèngzài zuò yí xiàng xīn de shìyàn.
example.english: The scientists are conducting a new experiment.
example.fact: 试验 (a controlled test or experiment) is a close cousin of 实验 — written with a different first character (试 "to try" vs. 实 "real, actual") but pronounced identically, shìyàn — a near-homophone pair that even native speakers sometimes mix up in casual writing, though usage leans toward 试验 for trials and 实验 for laboratory science.

examples.hanzi: 这次试验的结果很成功。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shìyàn de jiéguǒ hěn chénggōng.
examples.english: The result of this experiment was very successful.

examples.hanzi: 新药要经过很多次试验才能上市。
examples.pinyin: Xīn yào yào jīngguò hěn duō cì shìyàn cái néng shàngshì.
examples.english: A new drug must go through many tests before it reaches the market.

components.note: 丹 (cinnabar) — an ancient picture of a mine with cinnabar in it; 丹 is red, as in 牡丹.
尼 (ní) — 尼 sounds out 泥 ní and 呢 ní; here it appears mostly in foreign names such as 丹尼.

example.hanzi: 丹尼是我们班唯一的外国学生。
example.pinyin: Dānní shì wǒmen bān wéiyī de wàiguó xuésheng.
example.english: Danny is the only foreign student in our class.
example.fact: 丹尼 is a pure sound-based transliteration of the English name "Danny": 丹 (a red mineral pellet) and 尼 (used mainly in transliterations, as in 印度尼西亚, "Indonesia") were chosen for how they sound rather than for any meaning, a common way of rendering foreign personal names in Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 丹尼每天早上都去跑步。
examples.pinyin: Dānní měi tiān zǎoshang dōu qù pǎobù.
examples.english: Danny goes running every morning.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天跟丹尼一起看了球赛。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān gēn Dānní yìqǐ kàn le qiúsài.
examples.english: Yesterday I watched a ball game with Danny.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 作. 做 is a later variant of 作 zuò (to do), sharing its meaning and sound.
故 (gù) is only a loose sound hint.
夕 (evening, night) — night and time: 外, 多, 夜; dreams come at night, so 夕 is the meaning clue; 林 is only filler.

example.hanzi: 你想跟她结婚?你在做梦!
example.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng gēn tā jiéhūn? Nǐ zài zuòmèng!
example.english: You want to marry her? You're dreaming!
example.fact: Beyond literally "to dream" during sleep, 做梦 is just as often used figuratively to dismiss someone's unrealistic hope — 你在做梦 ("you're dreaming, in your dreams") — functioning almost exactly like the English idiom "keep dreaming," a rare case where the figurative sense translates nearly one-to-one.

examples.hanzi: 我昨晚做梦梦到自己在天上飞。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuówǎn zuòmèng mèngdào zìjǐ zài tiān shang fēi.
examples.english: Last night I dreamed that I was flying in the sky.

examples.hanzi: 别做梦了，快点起床上班吧！
examples.pinyin: Bié zuòmèng le, kuài diǎn qǐchuáng shàngbān ba!
examples.english: Stop daydreaming and get up for work!

components.note: 母 (mǔ) is a close sound clue for měi; the same part also in 海 hǎi, 梅 méi and 悔 huǐ.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 我们每年都会去海边旅行。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen měinián dōu huì qù hǎibiān lǚxíng.
example.english: We go on a trip to the beach every year.
example.fact: 每 ("every, each") pairs with almost any time or count word to build a whole family of "every-" expressions — 每天 ("every day"), 每次 ("every time"), 每个人 ("everyone") — and, like the quantifier 所有 ("all"), a 每-phrase is almost always followed later in the sentence by 都 ("without exception") to complete the sense.

examples.hanzi: 我每年夏天都回老家看爷爷奶奶。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi nián xiàtiān dōu huí lǎojiā kàn yéye nǎinai.
examples.english: Every summer I go back to my hometown to see my grandparents.

examples.hanzi: 这个节日每年都在十月举行。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiérì měi nián dōu zài shíyuè jǔxíng.
examples.english: This festival is held every October.
